results.title: Nonzero zero divisors
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, this is the set of elements $r \in R$ with $r \neq 0$ such that $sr = 0$ for some nonzero $s \in R$, that is, the nonzero zero divisors of $R$. They are the vertices of the zero-divisor graph of $R$.

results.title: The zero-divisor graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, the zero-divisor graph of $R$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the nonzero zero divisors of $R$, in which two distinct vertices $v$ and $w$ are adjacent exactly when $vw = 0$.

results.title: Vertices are the nonzero zero divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. An element $r \in R$ is a vertex of the zero-divisor graph of $R$ if and only if $r \neq 0$ and $r$ is a zero divisor, that is, $sr = 0$ for some nonzero $s \in R$.

results.title: Adjacency in the zero-divisor graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of the zero-divisor graph of $R$ are adjacent if and only if $v \neq w$ and $vw = 0$.

results.title: Odd-to-even ratio of $k$-full, $l$-free numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $2 \le k < l$. Call a natural number $n$ a $[k, l]$-integer if it is $k$-full and $l$-free, that is, $n \ge 1$ and every prime $p$ dividing $n$ satisfies $p^k \mid n$ and $p^l \nmid n$. For a natural number $N$ let $O_{k,l}(N)$ and $E_{k,l}(N)$ be the numbers of odd and of even $[k, l]$-integers $n \le N$. Then $O_{k,l}(N)/E_{k,l}(N) \to (2 - 2^{1 - 1/k})/(1 - 2^{1 - l/k})$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: Sequences with the same relative order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two finite sequences $s = s_1 \cdots s_\ell$ and $p = p_1 \cdots p_m$ of natural numbers have the same relative order if $\ell = m$ and, for all $1 \le i, j \le m$, $s_i < s_j$ holds if and only if $p_i < p_j$.

results.title: Classical pattern containment in a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $w$ of natural numbers contains the pattern $p = p_1 \cdots p_k$ if some subsequence $u_1 \cdots u_k$ of $w$ (whose entries need not be adjacent in $w$) has the same relative order as $p$: for all $a, b \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, $u_a < u_b$ if and only if $p_a < p_b$.

results.title: Consecutive pattern containment

results.title: Standardization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The standardization $\mathrm{st}(s)$ of a finite sequence $s = s_1 s_2 \cdots s_k$ of natural numbers is obtained by replacing each entry $s_i$ by the number of indices $j$ with $s_j \le s_i$. When the entries of $s$ are distinct, this number is the rank of $s_i$: the $r$th smallest entry becomes $r$.

results.title: Heads of runs of consecutive integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an optional previous entry $y$ and a sequence $s_1 s_2 \cdots s_\ell$ of natural numbers, this lists, in order, the entries $s_i$ with $s_i \ne s_{i-1} + 1$, where $s_0 = y$; if there is no previous entry, $s_1$ is always listed. With no previous entry, these are the minima $a$ of the maximal blocks $a, a + 1, \dots, a + k$ of adjacent consecutive integers of the sequence.

results.title: Reduction of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reduction $\operatorname{red}(s)$ of a finite sequence $s$ of natural numbers is obtained in two steps. First, every maximal block of adjacent entries of the form $a, a + 1, \ldots, a + k$ is replaced by its first entry $a$. Then the resulting sequence is standardized: each of its entries $x$ is replaced by the number of its entries that are at most $x$, which for distinct entries is the rank of $x$.

results.title: Standardization and reduction examples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The standardization of $315$ is $\mathrm{st}(315) = 213$, and the reduction of $16783425$ is $\mathrm{red}(16783425) = 15324$. Here $\mathrm{st}$ replaces each entry by its rank, and $\mathrm{red}$ replaces each maximal block of adjacent consecutive integers $a, a + 1, \dots, a + k$ by its minimum $a$ and then standardizes.

results.title: Push order of the superimpose operation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sequences $a$ and $b$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{push}(a, b)$ is the sequence obtained by taking the first entry of $b$, then the next two entries of $a$ (only one if just one is left), and repeating; once one of the two sequences is exhausted, the remaining entries of the other follow in order.

results.title: Superimpose operation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sequences $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ of natural numbers, let $p = \mathrm{push}(\mathrm{rev}\,\sigma_1, \mathrm{rev}\,\sigma_2)$ be the push order of the superimpose operation on the reversed sequences. Then $\mathrm{si}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2)$ is the reversal of $p$: the stack obtained by pushing the entries of $p$ in order onto an empty stack, read from top to bottom.

results.title: Suffix-tree search finds exactly the infixes

results.title: Up-step probability of the Moran process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Probability that one step of the Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative fitness `r` takes the mutant count from `i` to `i + 1`: a mutant is chosen to reproduce (probability `r i / (r i + N - i)`) and a wild type is chosen to die (probability `(N - i) / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N` (the real subtraction `N - i` is negative for `i > N`).

results.title: Down-step probability of the Moran process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Probability that one step of the Moran process takes the mutant count from `i` to `i - 1`: a wild type is chosen to reproduce (probability `(N - i) / (r i + N - i)`) and a mutant is chosen to die (probability `i / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N`.

results.title: Fixation probability of the Moran process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The fixation probability of the Moran process started from `i` mutants out of `N`: `(1 - r⁻¹ ^ i) / (1 - r⁻¹ ^ N)` for `r ≠ 1`, and `i / N` in the neutral case `r = 1`. The model's domain is `0 < r`, `N ≥ 1`, `i ≤ N`; outside it the value is the closed formula evaluated with Lean's total division (e.g. `x / 0 = 0`) and carries no meaning.

results.title: One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process on the states `Fin (N + 1)`: `a_i` to `i + 1`, `b_i` to `i - 1`, `1 - a_i - b_i` to `i`, and `0` elsewhere.

results.title: No up-step from the fixed state of the Moran process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No mutant can be added when the mutant type is fixed.

results.title: No down-step from the empty state of the Moran process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No mutant can be removed when the mutant type is absent.

results.title: Ratio of Moran down- and up-step probabilities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ratio of the down- and up-step probabilities is `1 / r`: `r · b_i = a_i`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran up-step probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The up-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran down-step probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The down-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

results.title: Moran up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N` the up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most `1`, so the probability `1 - a_i - b_i` of staying is nonnegative.

results.title: One-step expectation under the Moran process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One-step expectation of a function `f` of the mutant count from state `i`: `∑ j, P i j f j = a_i f (i + 1) + b_i f (i - 1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) f i` (the boundary terms vanish at `i = 0` and `i = N`).

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative fitness `r > 0`, as a stochastic matrix on the mutant counts `Fin (N + 1)`.

results.title: An absent mutant is never fixed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A mutant that is absent is never fixed: `φ_0 = 0`.

results.title: A fixed mutant stays fixed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A mutant that is already fixed stays fixed: `φ_N = 1` (for `N ≠ 0`).

results.title: First-step equation (Moran 1958)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fixation probability satisfies `φ_i = a_i φ_{i+1} + b_i φ_{i-1} + (1 - a_i - b_i) φ_i`. This is the first-step equation of the chain for the interior states `0 < i < N`; the identity is algebraic (it follows from `r · b_i = a_i`), so it is stated for every `i ≥ 1`.

results.title: Uniqueness of the fixation probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Any `ψ` with `ψ 0 = 0`, `ψ N = 1` that satisfies the first-step equation `ψ i = a_i ψ (i+1) + b_i ψ (i-1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) ψ i` at every `0 < i < N` equals `moranFixation r N` on `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.

results.title: Fixation probability of the chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain started at `i` is in state `N` after `t` steps tends to `φ_i` as `t → ∞`. Since `N` absorbs, this `t`-step probability is the probability of fixation by time `t`, so its limit is the probability of eventual fixation.

results.title: Loss probability of the chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain started at `i` is in state `0` after `t` steps tends to `1 - φ_i`; together with `tendsto_matPow_moranMatrix_last`, absorption at `0` or `N` is certain.

results.title: Pitman's merger rate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Pitman's merger rate `λ_{b,k} = ∫ x ^ (k - 2) (1 - x) ^ (b - k) Λ(dx)`: while there are `b` blocks, the rate at which a given set of `k` of them merges into one block, for `2 ≤ k ≤ b` (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1; Sagitov 1999). Powers are natural-number powers, so `0 ^ 0 = 1`. Outside `2 ≤ k ≤ b` no such merger exists, and the rate is defined to be `0`.

results.title: Total merger rate of a Λ-coalescent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total merger rate `λ_b = ∑_{k=2}^b (b.choose k) λ_{b,k}` while there are `b` blocks (Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

results.title: Generator of the Λ-coalescent block-counting process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generator of the block-counting process of the Λ-coalescent on the states `0, …, n` (state `b` means `b` blocks): from `b` blocks the process jumps to `j < b` blocks at rate `(b.choose (b + 1 - j)) λ_{b, b + 1 - j}` (a `(b + 1 - j)`-merger), and the diagonal is `-λ_b`. States `0` and `1` are absorbing (state `0` is never reached from `b ≥ 1`).

results.title: Nonnegativity of Λ-coalescent merger rates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Merger rates are nonnegative.

results.title: Pair merger rate of a Λ-coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two blocks merge at rate `Λ [0, 1]`; `Λ` is often normalized to a probability measure, so that this pair rate is `1` as in Kingman's coalescent.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the total merger rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total merger rate is nonnegative.

results.title: Λ-coalescent block-counting generator is a rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The block-counting generator is a rate matrix: its jump rates are nonnegative and each row sums to `0`, since the jump rates out of `b` blocks add up to `λ_b`.

results.title: Merger rates are bounded by the total mass of Λ
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A merger rate is at most the total mass of `Λ`.

results.title: Pitman's consistency relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pitman's consistency relation `λ_{b,k} = λ_{b+1,k} + λ_{b+1,k+1}` for `2 ≤ k ≤ b` (Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1): a given `k`-set of `b` blocks merges, with an extra block present, either without it or together with it.

results.title: Binomial identity behind the total merger rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The polynomial identity behind the closed form of the total merger rate: `x ^ 2 ∑_{k=2}^b (b.choose k) x ^ (k - 2) (1 - x) ^ (b - k) = 1 - (1 - x) ^ b - b x (1 - x) ^ (b - 1)` for every real `x` and every `b` (binomial theorem).

results.title: The total merger rate in closed form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total merger rate in closed form (Berestycki 2009, §3.1): `λ_b = (b.choose 2) Λ {0} + ∫_{(0,1]} (1 - (1 - x) ^ b - b x (1 - x) ^ (b - 1)) / x ^ 2 Λ(dx)`. The atom at `0` (the Kingman part) is split off, so no division by `0` occurs.

results.title: Recursion for the total merger rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding a block raises the total merger rate by `b λ_{b+1,2}`: `λ_{b+1} = λ_b + b λ_{b+1,2}`. The new events are exactly the binary mergers of the new block with one of the `b` old ones (a consequence of the consistency relation).

results.title: Monotonicity of the total merger rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total merger rate `λ_b` is nondecreasing in the number of blocks `b`.

results.title: Uniqueness in Pitman's representation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A finite measure on `[0, 1]` is determined by its merger rates; indeed by the rates `λ_{k,k} = ∫ x ^ (k - 2) Λ(dx)` of complete mergers, which are its moments (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1).

results.title: Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's coalescent is the Λ-coalescent with `Λ = δ₀`: only binary mergers occur, each pair merging at rate `1` (Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

results.title: Total merger rate of Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Kingman's coalescent the total merger rate is the number of pairs, `λ_b = b.choose 2`.

results.title: Merger rates of the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent (`Λ` = Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]`) has merger rates given by the Beta integral `λ_{b,k} = (k - 2)! (b - k)! / (b - 1)!` for `2 ≤ k ≤ b` (Bolthausen–Sznitman 1998; Pitman 1999; Berestycki 2009, §3.1).

results.title: Total merger rate of the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent the total merger rate is `λ_b = b - 1` (`b ≥ 1`).

results.title: Pitman's representation theorem, existence half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pitman's representation theorem, existence half (Pitman 1999, Theorem 1): every consistent family of nonnegative merger rates `r b k`, `2 ≤ k ≤ b`, is the family of merger rates `λ_{b,k}` of some finite measure `Λ` on `[0, 1]`. (Uniqueness of `Λ` is `LambdaCoalescent.eq_of_mergerRate_eq`.)
